title: Wienner
comment: Wienner — Classic reference: N Wiener, Extrapolation, Interpolation, and Smoothing of Stationary Time Series, 1949. Introduces Wiener interpolation (also known as Kriging) and filtering, which founded with C. Shannon modern communication theory. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiener_filter
alt_text: Wienner. Classic reference: N Wiener, Extrapolation, Interpolation, and Smoothing of Stationary Time Series, 1949. Introduces Wiener interpolation (also known as Kriging) and filtering, which founded with C. Shannon modern communication theory.

title: Svm
comment: Svm — Support vector machines maximize the classification margin for linear decision boundaries. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support-vector_machine
alt_text: Svm. Support vector machines maximize the classification margin for linear decision boundaries.

title: Marr
comment: Marr — Classic reference: D. Marr and E. Hildreth, Theory of edge detection, 1980. Laid out the foundations of low-level edge detection. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge_detection
alt_text: Marr. Classic reference: D. Marr and E. Hildreth, Theory of edge detection, 1980. Laid out the foundations of low-level edge detection.

title: Eigen Laplacian
comment: Eigen Laplacian — Eigenvectors of the Laplacian on compact planar domains define an orthogonal basis of oscillating functions, which generalize Fourier sinusoids. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet_eigenvalue
alt_text: Eigen Laplacian. Eigenvectors of the Laplacian on compact planar domains define an orthogonal basis of oscillating functions, which generalize Fourier sinusoids.

title: Marching Cube
comment: Marching Cube — Classic reference: W Lorensen, H Cline, Marching Cubes: A high resolution 3D surface construction algorithm, 1987. The standard algorithm to extract iso-curves/surfaces from a discretized image/volume. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_squares
alt_text: Marching Cube. Classic reference: W Lorensen, H Cline, Marching Cubes: A high resolution 3D surface construction algorithm, 1987. The standard algorithm to extract iso-curves/surfaces from a discretized image/volume.

title: Shepard
comment: Shepard — Shepard interpolation generalizes nearest neighbor interpolation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_distance_weighting
alt_text: Shepard. Shepard interpolation generalizes nearest neighbor interpolation.

title: Nesterov
comment: Nesterov — Classic reference: Y Nesterov, A method for solving a convex programming problem with convergence rate O(1/k^2). Improves the 1/k rate of vanilla gradient descent to 1/k^2. https://blogs.princeton.edu/imabandit/2013/04/01/acceleratedgradientdescent/
alt_text: Nesterov. Classic reference: Y Nesterov, A method for solving a convex programming problem with convergence rate O(1/k^2). Improves the 1/k rate of vanilla gradient descent to 1/k^2.

title: Fench Rock
comment: Fench Rock — Fenchel-Rockafellar duality leverages linear operators in Lagrange duality. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenchel%27s_duality_theorem
alt_text: Fench Rock. Fenchel-Rockafellar duality leverages linear operators in Lagrange duality.

title: Lotka
comment: Lotka — Classic reference: A. J. Lotka, Contribution to the Theory of Periodic Reaction, 1910. Lotka-Volterra is a non-linear ODE modeling chemical reaction or prey/predator behaviors which exhibits periodic solutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotka%E2%80%93Volterra_equations
alt_text: Lotka. Classic reference: A. J. Lotka, Contribution to the Theory of Periodic Reaction, 1910. Lotka-Volterra is a non-linear ODE modeling chemical reaction or prey/predator behaviors which exhibits periodic solutions.

title: Barron
comment: Barron — Multilayer perceptron with 1 hidden layer breaks the curse of dimensionality for Barron's functions. http://www.stat.yale.edu/~arb4/publications_files/UniversalApproximationBoundsForSuperpositionsOfASigmoidalFunction.pdf
alt_text: Barron. Multilayer perceptron with 1 hidden layer breaks the curse of dimensionality for Barron's functions.

title: Bertrand
comment: Bertrand — Classic reference: J. Bertrand, Theoreme relatif au mouvement d'un point attire vers un centre fixe, 1873. Only harmonic spring and gravity central forces produce periodic motions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand%27s_theorem
alt_text: Bertrand. Classic reference: J. Bertrand, Theoreme relatif au mouvement d'un point attire vers un centre fixe, 1873. Only harmonic spring and gravity central forces produce periodic motions.

title: Laplace Beltrami
comment: Laplace Beltrami — Wave equation on a surface. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_equation
alt_text: Laplace Beltrami. Wave equation on a surface.

title: Radiosity
comment: Radiosity — Classic reference: D Immel, M Cohen, D Greenberg, A radiosity method for non-diffuse environments, 1986. Describes conservation of light as an integral equation which is at the heart of global rendering techniques such as radiosity. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rendering_equation

title: Birkhoff
comment: Birkhoff — Birkhoff's contraction for Hilbert's metric is a key tool to quantify convergence of Markov-Chains (Perron-Frobenius). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_metric
alt_text: Birkhoff. Birkhoff's contraction for Hilbert's metric is a key tool to quantify convergence of Markov-Chains (Perron-Frobenius).

title: Metaballs
comment: Metaballs — Classic reference: J Blinn, A Generalization of Algebraic Surface Drawing, 1982. "Metaballs" are levelsets of mixtures of radial basis functions, which generate blobby lava-lamp-like behaviors. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaballs

title: Farthest Point
comment: Farthest Point — Classic reference: T Gonzalez, Clustering to minimize the maximum intercluster distance, 1985. Popularized the farthest point sampling greedy algorithm. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farthest-first_traversal
alt_text: Farthest Point. Classic reference: T Gonzalez, Clustering to minimize the maximum intercluster distance, 1985. Popularized the farthest point sampling greedy algorithm.

title: Eikonal
comment: Eikonal — The solution of the Eikonal equation is solved by advancing a front in the normal direction, similar to a grass fire. The most famous Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Refraction occurs when the speed has a discontinuity (Snell-Descart).
